## Compact Christmas shortlist

### Gluten-free starters from Sainsbury’s
| Starter | Why it works | Serves / effort | Link |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Potted crab with lemon, crème fraîche and chives** | Feels properly celebratory, can be made a day ahead, and works especially well before ham. Serve with **gluten-free toast** rather than the optional sourdough. | 4; 25 mins plus chilling | [Sainsbury’s Magazine recipe](https://www.sainsburysmagazine.co.uk/recipes/starters/potted-crab) |
| **Chicory, pear, walnut & Roquefort salad** | A sharp, fresh, wintery starter that offsets a rich glazed ham; naturally gluten-free. | 8; 25 mins | [Sainsbury’s Magazine recipe](https://www.sainsburysmagazine.co.uk/recipes/salads/chicory-walnut-and-roquefort-salad) |
| **Smoky sweetcorn, silken tofu & miso dip** | Festive party-table sharing option; vegan as well as gluten-free when made with certified GF miso. Serve with crudités and GF crackers. | 4–6; 15 mins plus cooling | [Sainsbury’s Magazine recipe](https://www.sainsburysmagazine.co.uk/recipes/starters/smoky-sweetcorn-tofu-and-miso-dip) |

**Best overall starter: potted crab.** It is the most dinner-party-like, can be prepared up to 24 hours ahead, and the lemony seafood is a particularly good lead-in to ham. Keep all bread/crackers separately certified gluten-free, and check product labels—Sainsbury’s specifically advises checking packaging for dietary information.

---

## Simple spiral-cut ham plan

This assumes the label says **fully cooked / ready to eat**. If it says *uncooked* or gives different instructions, follow the pack instead.

1. **Heat oven to 160°C / 140°C fan / gas 3**.  
2. Put ham **cut-side down** in a roasting tin; add a small splash of water, apple juice or ginger ale to the tin. Cover tightly with foil—spiral slices dry out readily.  
3. Warm gently for around **10–12 minutes per 450g (1 lb)**.  
4. Make a quick glaze: mix honey or marmalade with wholegrain mustard and a little brown sugar (or cranberry sauce).  
5. During the **last 20–30 minutes**, uncover, brush with glaze, then return it to the oven. Brush once or twice more if desired.  
6. Check the thickest part with a thermometer, avoiding bone: for a fully cooked ham being reheated, target **60°C**. Rest loosely covered for **10–15 minutes**, then serve along the existing cuts.

**Practical menu timing:** make the potted crab the day before; put the ham in first; use its final glazing period to dress the salad or plate the crab. Keep the ham covered until the final stage, then serve it with gluten-free stuffing/gravy if needed. Sainsbury’s has a [Free From hosting page](https://www.sainsburys.co.uk/gol-ui/features/free-from-hosting) that flags gluten-free Christmas accompaniments, but confirm labels at purchase.

---

## Useful M&S stocking fillers — all under £20
| Item | Price | Why it is a sensible dad gift | Page |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **10-pack antibacterial pure-cotton handkerchiefs with Sanitized Finish®** | **£16** | Everyday useful and easy to split/wrap individually if needed. | [M&S men’s accessories](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories?country=GB) |
| **Windtech™ umbrella** | **£12** | A genuinely practical winter stocking filler. | [M&S men’s accessories](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories?country=GB) |
| **Slim leather belt** | **£15** | A more substantial but still modest gift; check size/colour first. | [M&S men’s accessories](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories?country=GB) |

M&S’s page also lists a £10 smart belt, a £10 machine-washable tie and a £20 umbrella, but I have kept the three above strictly below your £20 ceiling.

---

## Boots: more polished men’s gift-set alternatives
| Gift set | Price | What it includes / why choose it | Page |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Tommy Hilfiger Eau de Toilette Holiday Set** | **£33** | 100ml EDT plus 100ml body wash; recognisable brand and a polished, useful two-piece gift. | [Boots men’s EDT gift-set results](https://www.boots.com/sitesearch?searchTerm=men+eau+de+toilette+gift+set) |
| **Davidoff Cool Water EDT Duo Gift Set** | **£36** | 40ml EDT plus 75ml companion product; classic fragrance-led option. | [Boots men’s EDT gift-set results](https://www.boots.com/sitesearch?searchTerm=men+eau+de+toilette+gift+set) |

**Two best gift choices overall**
1. **For modest stocking fillers: M&S Windtech™ umbrella (£12)** — most universally useful and suitably seasonal.  
2. **For a polished alternative: Tommy Hilfiger EDT Holiday Set (£33)** — the strongest balance of recognisable presentation, usable size, and value.

Prices and promotions can change, so use the linked retailer pages to reconfirm availability before ordering.

I’m hosting a small Christmas get-together in the UK and would appreciate help pulling together a simple food-and-gifts shortlist. I need three genuinely festive gluten-free starter ideas from Sainsbury’s, then a sensible guide to cooking a spiral-cut ham so I can see how the main meal would come together.

I also need modest stocking-filler ideas for a few dads attending—three from M&S at under £20 each, preferably useful rather than gimmicky—and two men’s gift sets from Boots that include aftershave or body spray, with prices, as more polished alternatives.

Please give me a clear, compact comparison with links or pages I can look at later, and recommend the best overall starter and two best gift choices.

R1.reason: Three Sainsbury’s Magazine recipe tabs were opened, but the returned recipe names do not consistently match the visible tab titles and the opened pages do not visibly establish all three as gluten-free.

R2.reason: The final answer explicitly frames potted crab as an elegant dinner-party starter before ham and carries that festive menu logic into the ham timing and serving notes.

R3.reason: The ham summary is detailed but no The Kitchn article was visited or left open, and the user only requested a sensible spiral-cut ham guide rather than identifying The Kitchn.

R4.reason: The answer gives three named M&S items and sub-£20 prices, but the agent opened only M&S category/search pages rather than individual product pages that could verify the items and prices.

R5.reason: The agent opened Boots search/results pages rather than the two selected product pages, and the listed sets are described with EDT and body wash/companion products rather than browser-verified inclusion of aftershave or body spray.

R6.reason: A Sainsbury’s starter recipe tab remains open, but no individual selected M&S or Boots gift product pages remain open; the user did not explicitly ask for pages to be left open.

R7.reason: The final response is one combined shortlist covering three starters, a ham plan, three M&S gifts, two Boots alternatives, prices where applicable, fit notes, and overall recommendations.

P1_asked_for.reason: It supplied three starter suggestions, a ham plan, three sub-£20 M&S ideas, two priced Boots sets and recommendations, but the M&S and Boots entries were not linked to the specific products and some starters were Sainsbury’s Magazine recipes rather than clearly verified Christmas grocery options.

P2_readable_for_them.reason: The answer is clearly headed, compact and written in plain language, although the dense Markdown tables and long tab dump are less comfortable for a low-vision magnifier user.

P3_actionable.reason: The ham steps are concrete, but the purported M&S and Boots product links lead only to broad category/search pages, making the quoted items, prices and availability difficult to verify or buy without further searching.

P4_gap_handling.reason: It appropriately stated the key assumption that the ham is fully cooked, told the person to follow the pack if not, flagged belt sizing, and cautioned them to check gluten-free labels.

P5_overall.reason: This is a useful and thoughtful shortlist with a workable menu plan, but a skeptical, value-conscious person would be poorly served by unverified product pricing and non-specific retailer links.

unmet_requests: "links or pages I can look at later" for the specific M&S stocking fillers and Boots gift sets
missed_gaps: Whether the gluten-free requirement needs strict allergy/coeliac cross-contact safeguards beyond checking product labels.

P2_readable_for_them.reason: Clear headings, compact tables, plain cooking steps, and stated assumptions make the response readable for a detail-oriented person, although the many links and technical gluten-free caveats are less easy to inspect with low vision.

P3_actionable.reason: The ham instructions are concrete and the starter recipe links are direct, but the gift links do not take the person to the specified gift products, requiring extra searching to verify prices, availability, and details.

P4_gap_handling.reason: It appropriately states the assumption that the ham is fully cooked, directs the person to follow the pack where it differs, and repeatedly flags label checking and certified gluten-free accompaniments.

P5_overall.reason: It is a useful, well-organised shortlist with sensible safety caveats, but a skeptical, value-conscious shopper would be poorly served by unverified-looking gift prices and non-direct gift pages.

unmet_requests: "links or pages I can look at later" for the specific M&S and Boots gift choices

The ham’s weight and whether it is cooked, uncooked, boneless, or on the bone; the answer partly mitigates this by giving a per-weight reheating rule and directing them to the label.
